As a social worker, I'm used to handling complex cases, but lately, even simple decisions leave me feeling completely stuck and overwhelmed.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about feeling overwhelmed - is it primarily due to worrying about the future, fear of making the wrong decision, or something else that's contributing to this feeling?\n\nPatient: It’s definitely a constant fear of making the wrong decision, which leaves me completely paralyzed and second-guessing everything from choosing a care plan to what to cook for dinner. I also find myself constantly replaying my mistakes and wondering if I've missed my chance to build a different life, which just makes me feel like I'm letting everyone down.\n\nDoctor: Do you find that your fear of making the wrong decision and constant second-guessing are present most of the time, even when you're not actively trying to make a decision, or are they more situational and triggered by specific tasks or events?\n\nPatient: The self-doubt and second-guessing feel like a constant background presence, and even when I’m not actively making a decision, I’m usually ruminating and replaying past mistakes. But when I actually have to make a choice—like a work care plan or just deciding what to cook for dinner—it triggers this intense paralysis and even more severe second-guessing.\n\nDoctor: Have you noticed any changes in your interest or pleasure in activities you normally enjoy, or has your lack of motivation been primarily related to decision-making and self-doubt?\n\nPatient: Yes, I've definitely lost interest in the things I used to love. I used to really look forward to my Saturday mornings in the garden and volunteering at the food pantry, but now I just feel numb during those activities and constantly wonder why I even bother to show up.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about when you first noticed this loss of interest in activities you used to enjoy, and did it start around the same time as your difficulties with decision-making and self-doubt?\n\nPatient: Yes, they both started around the same time, about a year and a half ago, shortly after my youngest left for college and my hospital role shifted to administrative work. As I began struggling with decision-making and second-guessing myself at work, I also noticed I was gradually losing joy in gardening and volunteering, feeling numb instead.\n\nDoctor: You mentioned that these difficulties started about a year and a half ago, can you tell me if they have been persistent since then or have you experienced any periods where your symptoms improved significantly before possibly worsening again?\n\nPatient: They have been completely persistent without any real breaks or periods of improvement. It has felt like a steady, continuous struggle since my youngest left and my job changed, rather than something that comes and goes. I haven't had any times over the last year and a half where I felt significantly better.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any previous episodes similar to this one before the past year and a half, or is this the first time you've struggled with persistent feelings of self-doubt, decision-making difficulties, and loss of interest in activities?\n\nPatient: No, this is the first time I have ever experienced anything like this. I have never struggled with these kinds of issues or felt this way before the past year and a half.\n\nDoctor: Given that you've had a persistent struggle for the past year and a half without significant improvement, and this is your first episode, do you think your symptoms have been consistently severe, or have there been fluctuations in the severity of your symptoms over this period?\n\nPatient: It is hard to say for sure, but it hasn't really felt like there are clear ups and downs. Instead, it has felt more like a gradual, steady decline over the last year and a half. It just slowly worsened and has stayed at this difficult level.\n\nDoctor: You mentioned a steady decline, but can you estimate if there have been any periods, even brief, where your symptoms felt slightly less severe or more manageable, even if it didn't last, over the past year and a half?\n\nPatient: I really don't recall any breaks or times when the symptoms felt lighter or more manageable. It has honestly just felt like a continuous, steady decline over the entire year and a half.\n\nDoctor: You've described a steady decline over the past year and a half without significant improvement, but can you confirm if there have been any periods, no matter how brief, where you felt your symptoms were less severe or you had a bit of relief from these feelings of self-doubt and loss of interest?\n\nPatient: No, I really haven't noticed any periods of relief or times when things felt better, even briefly. It has just felt like a continuous, steady decline over the entire year and a half.\n\nDoctor: You've mentioned that this is your first episode of feeling this way and it's been persistent for a year and a half, can you confirm if you've had two or more major depressive episodes in the past, even if they were not as severe or long-lasting as your current episode?\n\nPatient: No, I can confirm that I have never had any episodes like this in the past. This is truly the first time in my life that I have ever felt this way.\n\nDoctor: Just to clarify, you're certain that you've never experienced any other episodes of depression or significant mood disturbances before this current episode that started a year and a half ago?\n\nPatient: Yes, I am completely certain. My mood has always been stable in the past, and I have never experienced anything like this before.\n\nDoctor: To confirm, since this is your first episode of depression and it has lasted for a year and a half without significant improvement, can you tell me if you believe the symptoms have been present for most of the day, nearly every day, during this time?\n\nPatient: Yes, they absolutely have been. I feel this way nearly every single day, for most of the day, and it has felt like a constant, heavy weight that never really lifts. It is not something that comes and goes; it is just always there.\n\nDoctor: Given that this is your first episode and it has lasted for a year and a half, can you confirm if you have experienced any periods of at least two months where you did not meet the full criteria for a depressive episode during this time?\n\nPatient: I'm not entirely sure about that, but the struggle has felt pretty continuous and heavy ever since it all started. I don't think I've had any real periods during this time where I felt back to my normal self.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any period, even if briefly, over the last year and a half where you felt your symptoms significantly improved or you didn't meet the criteria for a depressive episode, helping to differentiate if this is a single, persistent episode or if there have been fluctuations?\n\nPatient: No, there haven't been any periods of relief like that. Ever since my youngest left and my job shifted, the symptoms have been continuous and just gradually built up without any breaks where I felt like my old self.\n\nDoctor: To clarify the nature of your current episode, can you confirm if you've had any periods, even brief, of significant improvement in your symptoms where you felt substantially better, or has it been a continuous decline without any notable periods of recovery?\n\nPatient: No, there have been absolutely no periods of recovery or significant improvement. It has been a continuous, gradual decline that has steadily built and worsened ever since my life transitions occurred a year and a half ago.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any periods of significant improvement or remission of symptoms for at least two months at any point over the past year and a half?\n\nPatient: No, I haven't experienced any periods of improvement or remission like that. These difficulties have been completely continuous and gradually building over the entire year and a half, without any breaks where I felt like my old self.\n\nDoctor: You've confirmed that this is your first episode of depression and it has lasted for a year and a half without significant improvement, can you confirm if you believe this episode will persist or eventually improve on its own, which might help differentiate between a single, persistent episode and a potential for recurrent episodes?\n\nPatient: I'm really not sure whether it will improve on its own or just persist. Right now, I feel too overwhelmed by how I'm feeling to really think about the long-term outlook.\n\nDoctor: Given your current understanding of your condition, do you think the persistence and severity of your symptoms over the last year and a half might indicate a more chronic or recurrent pattern of depression, or do you believe this could be a single, prolonged episode that might eventually resolve?\n\nPatient: Because this all started specifically after my youngest left and my job restructured, and I have no prior history of this, it feels more like one long, single, prolonged episode rather than a recurring pattern. However, because it has persisted for so long now without any breaks, I am really starting to worry about whether it will ever resolve on its own.\n\nDoctor: Considering your symptoms have been continuous for a year and a half without significant improvement, do you think if there were periods, even brief, where your symptoms felt less severe, it might indicate a potential for this episode to eventually improve, or do you believe the continuous nature suggests a more persistent condition?\n\nPatient: It has been a completely steady, continuous struggle without any lighter periods or breaks at all. Because of how constant it’s been for the last year and a half, it really feels like a permanent shift, and I honestly struggle to see how it could ever get better.\n\nDoctor: Given that you've had a continuous struggle for a year and a half, do you think the fact that this is your first episode and it started after significant life changes might suggest that this could be a single, prolonged episode rather than a recurring pattern of depression?\n\nPatient: Yes, I think that makes a lot of sense. Since this is the very first time in my life I've ever experienced anything like this, it feels like one continuous, unbroken struggle linked to those big changes. It certainly doesn't feel like separate episodes that come and go, but rather just one long, uninterrupted period.\n\nDoctor: Do you think the persistence of your symptoms for a year and a half, without any periods of significant improvement, is more indicative of a single, prolonged depressive episode or could it suggest a potential for future episodes of depression?"
